general_information.Description: Description: This course will give you a thorough explanation of how media technologies develop, operate, converge, and affect society in order to think critically about the media and its effects on culture. It provides a comprehensive introduction to today's global media environment and the ongoing developments in technology, culture, and critical theory that continue to transform this rapidly evolving industry and affect your everyday life. Our emphasis is on the social relations of power and connectivity that are shaped by new media as practices of communication. Specific topics that will be explored include: the latest developments and trends in social media, e-publishing, policy changes for Internet governance, online privacy protection, online ad exchanges, the changing video game industry, and much more. By studying this course, students will develop knowledge and skills in creative thinking, communication, collaboration, planning, critical analysis, and digital and ethical citizenship. Teaching methods: Direct Instruction, Inquiry-based Learning, Cooperative Learning, Case Study Analysis
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify how media technologies develop, operate, converge, and affect societys in order to develop expertise in creating the type of digital content that is widely in demand
Demonstrate the changing process of media and clarify how technology, culture and media career have altered in the era of new media
Identify career path related to new media technologies that best fits your skills and strengths
Discover the development of Web and Media in the digital age
Define the relationship between Public Relations, Advertising and the media in the past and at the moment.
Analyse media and its impact on communication and society.
Understand how to apply media ethics, policy and regulatory frameworks to create media content

constructive_questions.Name: QN1.1
constructive_questions.Details: How would you tell the story of the development of the information society to your parents?

constructive_questions.Name: QN2.1
constructive_questions.Details: Describe what convergence has meant in your life and how it affects you?

constructive_questions.Name: QN3.1
constructive_questions.Details: Explain the key features of the digital era and the concept of media convergence.

constructive_questions.Name: QN3.2
constructive_questions.Details: What will your future life in the information society be like?

constructive_questions.Name: QN4.1
constructive_questions.Details: Does the SMCR model adequately explain social media?

constructive_questions.Name: QN11.1
constructive_questions.Details: Debate the following proposition: books are an obsolete medium?

constructive_questions.Name: QN12.1
constructive_questions.Details: How has the content of magazines changed over time, and why?

constructive_questions.Name: QN13.1
constructive_questions.Details: What is news for you? And what should be news?

constructive_questions.Name: QN14.1
constructive_questions.Details: Go through your local newspaper-in print, on the Internet, or mobile device and de scribe the objective of each section. How do local newspapers differ from national ones in content?

constructive_questions.Name: QN15.1
constructive_questions.Details: How is recent technology changing the way print media is produced, distributed, and read? Is this a good thing?

constructive_questions.Name: QN16.1
constructive_questions.Details: Why do most people prefer getting their news from a traditional news organization (whether in print or digital) with an editor than searching online or reading a blog?

constructive_questions.Name: QN20.1
constructive_questions.Details: How does the history of popular music help us understand where music is going as a business? As artistic statements? As politics?

constructive_questions.Name: QN22.1
constructive_questions.Details: What can other media industries learn from the challenge digital media and Internet dis tribution created for the music industry?

constructive_questions.Name: QN23.1
constructive_questions.Details: Do you think broadcast radio still plays a positive role in helping people like you learn about new music? If not, what if anything should be done about it?

constructive_questions.Name: QN23.2
constructive_questions.Details: The United States was the first country to turn radio into a commercial medium. What does that tell us about how new media will develop in the United States? How might they be different elsewhere?

constructive_questions.Name: QN24.1
constructive_questions.Details: How does the history of radio help us understand how Internet radio, podcasting, and other audio media are going to develop as commercial forms? As artistic forms?

constructive_questions.Name: QN27.1
constructive_questions.Details: How does the history of film help us understand how movies will develop as they interact or converge with parts of the Internet, like iTunes distribution or Netflix?

constructive_questions.Name: QN28.1
constructive_questions.Details: Do you think that the impact of special effects and other technology on films is positive?

constructive_questions.Name: QN29.1
constructive_questions.Details: Do the new tools help or harm storytelling in film?

constructive_questions.Name: QN30.1
constructive_questions.Details: Does violence in film need to be more tightly controlled?

constructive_questions.Name: QN31.1
constructive_questions.Details: How do you assess your options for future TV viewing? If you had to buy a TV right now that would meet your needs in 2022, what would you buy?

constructive_questions.Name: QN32.1
constructive_questions.Details: Pitch your idea for a YouTube video. Think about what would make it appeal to 18- to 34-year-olds since that is a group that advertisers prize. Make it good if you want to be discovered by Hollywood!

constructive_questions.Name: QN37.1
constructive_questions.Details: What would be the best way to govern the Internet in the future? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: QN38.1
constructive_questions.Details: How do you explain the waning popularity of social media like Facebook among college students?

constructive_questions.Name: QN38.2
constructive_questions.Details: Analyze your online privacy and security practices, and outline a plan for making yourself safer online?

constructive_questions.Name: QN39.1
constructive_questions.Details: Are smartphones and tablets making PCs and TVs obsolete?

constructive_questions.Name: QN40.1
constructive_questions.Details: How has your smartphone changed your life for better? For worse?

constructive_questions.Name: QN41.1
constructive_questions.Details: What will your mobile phone be like in 2020?

constructive_questions.Name: QN42.1
constructive_questions.Details: Now that you know your cell phone is a threat to your privacy, what will you do?

constructive_questions.Name: QN43.1
constructive_questions.Details: Debate the following statement: sexist video games should be banned for children?

constructive_questions.Name: QN43.2
constructive_questions.Details: What should a government do to manage sexual contents?

constructive_questions.Name: QN45.1
constructive_questions.Details: What would you say is the most important effect the media have had on your life?

constructive_questions.Name: QN45.2
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss ways that people can benefit from the media nowsadays?

constructive_questions.Name: QN46.1
constructive_questions.Details: What should the government do to protect children from harmful media content?

constructive_questions.Name: QN46.2
constructive_questions.Details: Is it true that exposure to violent TV harms young children? Explain your answer.

constructive_questions.Name: QN47.1
constructive_questions.Details: Why and how has PR become a profession over the years?

constructive_questions.Name: QN48.1
constructive_questions.Details: Let's say a client wants to hire your agency. The only problem is that you don't agree with their ethics. What would you do and why?

constructive_questions.Name: QN49.1
constructive_questions.Details: What were the most important developments that led to the advertising industry of today?

constructive_questions.Name: QN49.2
constructive_questions.Details: What do you think about the roles of social media (Facebook, Tiktok, etc.) in the advertising industry?

constructive_questions.Name: QN50.1
constructive_questions.Details: Advertising receives substantial criticism, so let's accentuate the positive: what are the good things that advertising does for you and for society?

constructive_questions.Name: QN50.2
constructive_questions.Details: What do you think about a concept of "sustainable advertising"?

constructive_questions.Name: QN57.1
constructive_questions.Details: What is globalization?

constructive_questions.Name: QN58.1
constructive_questions.Details: Why do people characterize the media relations between countries and cultures in the past 20 years as increasing globalization?

constructive_questions.Name: QN60.1
constructive_questions.Details: What do you think about "The Great Firewall of China"?
